proof.observed: Every row --- PASS, ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/workflow 6.088s: after the late push the issue is in implementing from testing (start waits on the tester), reviewing (reviewer), retro (nobody) and merging (merger), each with a checks-red naming the from-phase; in awaiting_merge the verdict reads red by the carry and the issue stays with no notice, no supervise row and no merge-queue publish. The probe: in implementing and production_check the issue stays, no notice, no supervise row, no counted round, and the push fact is not refused (transition finds no row and returns nil).
proof.negativeControl: At 9fb30a6c the same red test fails its testing, retro and merging rows ('after the late push completed the carry the issue is in testing, want implementing') and passes reviewing (round 1's failures entry).

risks: D2's daemon side (probe, not pinned): after a red moves retro to implementing, an implementer completion reporting any commit but its last handoff is accepted as the implementation's and moves the issue to testing; HANDOFF_NOT_NEW catches only the last handoff commit. The refusal of a retro completion rests on pi-legion's lookup of implement.json at the state's phase, read before the commit is found and the completion posted, so a red landing inside that window lets a retro completion through. Narrow; recorded for the architect, no change asked.

A red standing when a phase is entered is not re-read (plan D4): an implementer that completes on a code head already red, its handoff push and synchronize known, hands the tester a head whose verdict is red with nothing to act on it until the next CI fact or READY. Accepted by the plan; noted because the failure above is the neighbouring case where the daemon learns of the red after entry.

Local lanes: the NATS-backed tests were skipped by name per the LEGION-668 recipe; CI's Tests run 38521728279 ran them at 8593a1a1. go.work.sum was rewritten by the CLI build and restored before committing.

failures.evidence: A push classified after its head arrived, which completes the carry of a code head's red to the handoff head that replaced it (classify.SettlementFor, carriedBack), sends the work back only in reviewing: workflow/pullrequest.go's push handler returns before standingRed when issue.Phase != phase.Reviewing (the guard that also gates reaskRound), so in testing, retro and merging the issue stays where it is with classify.HeadVerdict red for its head and no checks-red, no implementer start and no counted round. The implementer's own standingRed doc names a push classified late as one of the two non-CI facts that apply the rule, and no test had a row for it outside reviewing. Live path: the implementer's handoff push (implement.json) whose webhook reaches the daemon after the synchronize and after the implementer's completion moved the issue to testing, with the code head's red already recorded in implementing. Pinned by packages/daemon/internal/workflow/checks_red_test.go TestAPushClassifiedLateThatCompletesTheCarryOfARedSendsTheWorkBackFromEveryPhase (commit 881481d11a0e): LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:54332/postgres?sslmode=disable go -C packages/daemon test -count=1 ./internal/workflow -run TestAPushClassifiedLateThatCompletesTheCarryOfARedSendsTheWorkBackFromEveryPhase -v → --- FAIL testing (after the late push completed the carry the issue is in testing, want implementing), --- FAIL retro, --- FAIL merging, --- PASS reviewing. Applying standingRed before the reviewing guard (reaskRound stays reviewing's) in a scratch copy of the branch makes the test pass and leaves the whole workflow package green (go test ./internal/workflow -skip 'Consume|Captured|RateLimited|BackwardMoveNoRow|LateEventOfAnEarlier': ok, 82s); the implementer owns the fix.
